Every estimate refetches live FAL pricing, and during a FAL outage it shows "Estimate unavailable", which is the #111 outage case coming back through the custom-rate path. Pass `endpoint_id` here as well, and add a test that combines a custom rate with a FAL outage.

findings.finding: **note** `electron/commands/http.ts:78` The dispatcher with no inactivity timeout is chosen because the caller passes `timeout_ms`, not because of which host is called. findings.resolution: HttpRequestArgs documents any-host opt-in semantics, one-hour total cap and why ordinary cloud calls must leave timeout_ms unset.

findings.finding: **fix** `src/components/ProjectBibleView.tsx:287-315,516-544` The creation draft key is only cleared on success or Clear, so recovering the entry another way doesn't release it. To reproduce: the "Mara" generation fails and leaves an empty entry. The user recovers Mara through Variation or Upload in her details. Later they type "Bob" in the composer and click Generate, and `updateBibleAsset` renames Mara (picture included) to Bob and adds Bob's picture to her. Frames do the same with `rules_json`. Only reuse the entry while it has no variants, or drop the key once a picture lands. Separately, the rename spreads a cached `asset` instead of the current row.
findings.resolution: Creation retries reuse only a current entry with no takes. Recovering through Variation or Upload releases the draft identity; character/location/frame regressions and a manual recovery/new-entry journey passed.

findings.finding: **fix** `electron/main.ts` There is no `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` or `second-instance` handler (still missing with every fix PR combined). On Windows and Linux, double-clicking a `.showbiz` file or a recent item while Showbiz is running starts a second process. That process opens the legacy `showbiz.db` concurrently and starts a second MCP bridge, and if the file is already open it shows "already open or its lock cannot be verified". Take the single-instance lock, quit if it isn't acquired, and feed `projectFileArguments(argv)` from `second-instance` into `projectFiles.add`.
findings.resolution: Official Electron requestSingleInstanceLock/second-instance pattern routes subsequent arguments to current window before duplicate runtime startup. Relative paths use launcher cwd; restore/focus covered. Independent instances remain possible with separate profiles/device-storage directories.

findings.finding: **fix** `electron/project-cache.ts:27` `JSON.parse` of a marker can throw inside the loop, and the catch wraps the whole sweep. A crash between `mkdtemp` and the marker write leaves an empty `.owner.json`. After that, every startup shows a warning, never deletes that folder, and stops before reaching any later `open-*` folder, so abandoned caches pile up again. Handle errors per entry and keep going.
findings.resolution: Cache sweep isolates and reports errors per entry. This process identity is cached; other owners remain independently verified. An atomic mkdir guard serializes abandoned-lock reclamation, with native permission codes preserved.

findings.finding: **fix** `electron/process-owner.ts:53-60` `createProcessOwner()` re-checks this process's own identity on every lock and every workspace. On Windows and macOS that runs `powershell.exe`/`ps` synchronously on the main process, with 3s/2s timeouts, so every New, Open or Save As on Windows freezes the UI for two PowerShell startups. Our own identity never changes: compute it once.
findings.resolution: Cache sweep isolates and reports errors per entry. This process identity is cached; other owners remain independently verified. An atomic mkdir guard serializes abandoned-lock reclamation, with native permission codes preserved.

findings.finding: **note** `electron/project-document-lock.ts:25-32` If two instances both see the same dead lock, both delete it: the second deletes the first one's fresh lock and writes its own. The loser's release then throws after `dispose` has already closed the DB. Rare, but the reclaim should be atomic (write a temp lock and rename it into place), and the lock should be released before the DB closes.
findings.resolution: The competing-reclaimer race is fixed with an atomic mkdir guard. The database intentionally closes before releasing ownership so another writer cannot enter while the old connection remains open. A temp-file rename alone would not provide compare-and-swap protection.

findings.finding: **fix** `electron/mcp/contract.ts:5` (`socket: z.string()`) with `sessions.ts:71-77` `list_sessions` now connects to every descriptor's `socket` path automatically and sends the bearer secret. Before this PR, that only happened on an explicit attach. On Windows the owner/mode check (`sessions.ts:40`) doesn't apply. Anything that can write into `SHOWBIZ_MCP_DIR` can plant a descriptor pointing at a UNC pipe (`\\host\pipe\x`), and every listing would then connect out over SMB and could leak NTLM credentials. Validate the path when parsing: `\\.\pipe\showbiz-${id}` on win32, and the `tmpdir()/showbiz-mcp-XXXXXX/app.sock` shape that `removeStaleSocket` already expects on POSIX.
findings.resolution: Descriptor schema validates exact local Windows pipe ID or private Showbiz POSIX temporary socket namespace before discovery probing.

findings.finding: **note** `sessions.ts:96-108` Echoing id/pid defeats PID reuse, but it doesn't prove who the server is, since both values come from the descriptor. That protection still comes from the 0700 socket directory. The "authenticated instance-health" wording could say so.
findings.resolution: MCP guide separates ID/PID freshness from private-socket directory and bearer-secret access protection.

findings.finding: **note** `sessions.ts:130-155` `removeStaleSocket` has no test, because the liveness test socket sits outside `tmpdir()`. If the adapter runs with a different `TMPDIR` from the app, cleanup is skipped silently.
findings.resolution: Stale liveness test uses an actual private tmpdir/showbiz-mcp-XXXXXX/app.sock path and asserts folder removal; guide explicitly requires shared TMPDIR and rejects foreign namespaces.

findings.finding: **fix** `electron/commands/generation-billing.ts:25-28,157` The `retryAfter` cooldown map stores the raw FAL/OpenRouter API key (`key: credentials.get(row.provider)`) for up to 500 entries, for as long as the main process runs. That breaks the "keys fetched per call and discarded" rule (CLAUDE.md, docs/architecture.md), and the keys would show up in any heap snapshot, crash dump or future debug log of the map. Store a hash of the key (e.g. SHA-256) and compare that instead.
findings.resolution: Cooldown entries retain SHA-256 credential fingerprints. API keys remain local to the active reconciliation call. Security regression inspects retained entry allocations; existing key-change/cooldown behavior remains tested.

findings.finding: **fix** `electron/project-documents.ts:182-184,209-210` The media archive that gets restored and synced is a throwaway one built for the temp DB. The active document gets a fresh `createDocumentMedia` from `prepare()`, and its `stamps` map starts empty (`project-document-media.ts:17`). Before this PR, Save As and conversion used the document's own archive. Result: the first edit after New Project, Save As or library conversion deletes and rewrites every embedded media blob on the main thread, which means a long freeze and a full file rewrite on a multi-GB project. Pass the populated archive (or its stamps) into `prepare`.
findings.resolution: The populated archive is rebound to the reopened database with its fingerprints. Tests and a separate runtime API demo prove first edits after conversion/Save As do not rewrite unchanged media.

findings.finding: **note** `electron/mcp/session.ts:174-184,207-210` Only successful results are cached for replay. If an export fails after the agent's wait already hit `TIMEOUT`, the agent retries with the same request ID as `docs/mcp.md` tells it to, a second save dialog opens, and the first error is never seen. Either cache terminal failures for the active ID or soften the docs.
findings.resolution: Terminal Result and thrown export failures cached under request ID; regression confirms one dispatch through PENDING and replay.

findings.finding: **note** `electron/mcp/sessions.ts:147` The `TIMEOUT` message tells reads to "retry with the same request ID", but reads don't have one.

findings.finding: **note** `electron/project-documents.ts:140-147` The "referenced media could not be included" check after sync can no longer trigger, because `sync()` either embeds every referenced file or throws ENOENT first. qualifications: Published commit histories are retained; no amend, rebase or force push. Historical phase/grouping criticism cannot be repaired retroactively.
PR139 is superseded by142 and closed. Dependencies remain explicit; no PR was merged into dev.
Legacy conversion still rejects missing referenced media instead of silently dropping takes. The original library remains untouched.
FAL historical per-request averages are not settings-specific unit calculations. Billable quantities are not inferred from ambiguous unit labels.
A crash during short-lived lock reclamation can leave a guard. Close all instances before removing the named guard.
MCP discovery requires the same temporary namespace; native Windows ACL and macOS window behavior were not manually verified.
Metadata-only licence exceptions are explicit; complete legal text is not invented for packages that do not publish it.
